encoding.rationale: isinstance(op, str) tests the runtime Python type of op, which is not an integer/boolean/comparison over scalar inputs. We abstract op's type to an EnumSort TypeTag in {STR, CALLABLE} and encode the predicate as (op_type == STR). The seeded enum values map: 'Add' -> a str literal (STR tag), '<lambda>' -> a callable (CALLABLE tag, __name__=='<lambda>').
encoding.verified: z3 Solver().check() == sat for both pred and Not(pred); runtime isinstance() confirms 'Add'->True, lambda->False.

true_examples.op_concrete: the Python str 'Add' (any FuncMap key; derived in production from type(node.op).__name__)
true_examples.taken_branch: true (op treated as operator name; assert op in FuncMap; func = FuncMap[op])
true_examples.proven_by: z3 model op_type=STR AND runtime isinstance('Add', str) == True

false_examples.op_concrete: a callable, e.g. (lambda lhs, rhs: lhs + rhs) whose __name__ == '<lambda>'
false_examples.proven_by: z3 model op_type=CALLABLE AND runtime isinstance(<lambda>, str) == False

crosshair.detail: crosshair check on op_is_name returned 'Targets found, but contain no checkable functions' (exit 0). The helper is a pure type predicate with no asserts/contracts to refute, so CrossHair has nothing to disprove. Absence of a counterexample here is NOT a proof; the True/False witnesses are established by direct z3 model + runtime evaluation.

notes: Classification is runtime-dependent: the branch is decided by the live Python type of op, not by any CLI flag, YAML key, env var, filesystem, or GPU probe. isinstance and str are builtins, not injectable.

In ALL production ExpressionEvaluator paths op is a str (type(node.op).__name__ / type(node.ops[i]).__name__ / evaluate(node.func)), so the TRUE branch is always taken in production. The FALSE branch is reachable only when createBinaryOp is invoked directly with a callable (test/direct API usage), per the Slice fragment.

z3 was actually run in-container (real model output: op_type=STR for true, op_type=CALLABLE for false). The type-tag encoding abstracts a Python isinstance test, so it is solver-backed only under the assumption op's type ranges over {str, callable}; the seeded domain matches. Because the underlying decision is a live-object type test rather than scalar arithmetic, the overall classification remains runtime-dependent.
Witnesses pinned by VALUE so downstream can reify behavior: pass op='Add' (any FuncMap key) for true; pass a lambda for false.
